_about: What each move in a curated workout works (area) and why it's there (job), plus a short 'for your goal' note per kind of workout. Areas follow the Free Exercise DB's primary muscles, in plain words. A job that rests on a study names it in 'research'; every id must be verified in research.json. Goal notes say what a workout can and can't do. 'expect' is shown under every goal note.

90/90 Hamstring.job: Stretches the back of the thigh.

Adductor/Groin.job: Stretches the inner thighs for wider, easier hip movement.

Ankle Circles.job: Circles the ankle to move it through its range.

Arm Circles.job: Moves the shoulders through their range to warm them up.

Barbell Bench Press - Medium Grip.job: Presses weight up from your chest: the main upper-body pushing lift.

Barbell Deadlift.job: Lifts a bar from the floor using legs, hips and back together; it works your core hard too.

Barbell Hip Thrust.job: Drives loaded hips up from a bench: a direct, heavy glute move.

Barbell Squat.job: Bends hips and knees together: the main lower-body strength pattern; squats work your core too.

Bench Dips.job: Lowers and pushes your body up using your arms.

Bent Over Barbell Row.job: Pulls toward your body, strengthening the upper back for posture.

Bodyweight Squat.job: Bends hips and knees together: the main lower-body strength pattern; squats work your core too.

Bodyweight Walking Lunge.area: Thighs and glutes, one leg at a time
Bodyweight Walking Lunge.job: Trains each leg on its own, for strength and balance.

Butt Lift (Bridge).job: Drives your hips up, working the glutes with the knees bent.

Cat Stretch.job: Rounds and arches the back to move the whole spine.

Chest And Front Of Shoulder Stretch.job: Opens the chest after sitting or pressing.

Child's Pose.job: Rests the hips back to stretch the lower back.

Cross-Body Crunch.job: Curls and twists your ribs toward the opposite knee.

Dead Bug.job: Keeps your lower back down while your arms and legs move (anti-extension).

Decline Push-Up.job: Pushes your body away from the floor; your core holds you straight.

Dips - Triceps Version.job: Lowers and pushes your body up using your arms.

Dumbbell Bench Press.job: Presses weight up from your chest: the main upper-body pushing lift.

Dumbbell Lunges.area: Thighs and glutes, one leg at a time
Dumbbell Lunges.job: Trains each leg on its own, for strength and balance.

Dumbbell Rear Lunge.area: Thighs and glutes, one leg at a time
Dumbbell Rear Lunge.job: Trains each leg on its own, for strength and balance.

Dumbbell Step Ups.area: Thighs and glutes, one leg at a time
Dumbbell Step Ups.job: Pushes your body up onto a step with one leg: strength and balance for stairs.

Face Pull.area: Back of the shoulders and upper back
Face Pull.job: Pulls a rope toward your face, balancing all the pressing.

Freehand Jump Squat.area: Thighs and glutes, raises heart rate
Freehand Jump Squat.job: Jumping moves: leg power and a fast heart rate.

Front Dumbbell Raise.job: Lifts the arms forward to shoulder height.

Front Leg Raises.job: Swings the leg forward to loosen the hamstrings and hips.

Full Range-Of-Motion Lat Pulldown.area: Lats (sides of the back) and biceps
Full Range-Of-Motion Lat Pulldown.job: Pulls a bar down from overhead: the move that builds toward a pull-up.

Glute Kickback.job: Pushes one leg back and up, working one glute at a time.

Goblet Squat.job: Bends hips and knees together: the main lower-body strength pattern; squats work your core too.

Hammer Curls.job: A curl with thumbs up, which also works the forearm.

Hanging Leg Raise.job: Lifts your legs while you hang, working the six-pack muscle and the front of your hips.

Inchworm.job: Walks the hands out to a plank and back: a moving stretch for the back of the legs.

Incline Dumbbell Press.job: Presses on an inclined bench, with more work for the upper chest and front shoulders.

Incline Push-Up Close-Grip.job: Hands close and raised: an easier push-up angle that puts more work on the triceps.

Inverted Row.job: Pulls toward your body, strengthening the upper back for posture.

Kneeling Hip Flexor.job: Stretches the front of the hip, which gets tight from sitting.

Leg Extensions.job: Straightens the knee against resistance, isolating the front of the thigh.

Leg Press.job: Bends hips and knees together: the main lower-body strength pattern; squats work your core too.

Lying Glute.job: Stretches the glutes and the outside of the hip.

Lying Leg Curls.job: Bends the knee against resistance, isolating the back of the thigh.

Mountain Climbers.area: Core and legs, raises heart rate
Mountain Climbers.job: Holds a plank while your knees drive in fast: core control plus a quick sweat.

One-Arm Dumbbell Row.job: Pulls toward your body, strengthening the upper back for posture.

Pelvic Tilt Into Bridge.job: Rolls your spine up one bone at a time, for control of your lower back and hips.

Pike Push-Up.job: Pushes with your hips high, so the shoulders press overhead like in a handstand.

Plank.job: Holds your body in one straight line so your back doesn't sag (anti-extension).

Push Up to Side Plank.job: A push-up, then a turn into a side plank: pushing strength plus obliques.

Push-Up Wide.job: Pushes your body away from the floor; your core holds you straight.

Pushups.job: Pushes your body away from the floor; your core holds you straight.

Reverse Crunch.job: Curls your hips up toward your ribs, working the six-pack muscle from the bottom.

Reverse Flyes.job: Opens the arms out behind you, balancing all the pressing.

Romanian Deadlift.job: Hinges at the hips with a long stretch on the back of the thighs.

Runner's Stretch.job: Stretches the back of the thigh.

Scapular Pull-Up.job: Hangs and pulls the shoulder blades down without bending the arms: the first step toward a pull-up.

Scissors Jump.area: Thighs and glutes, raises heart rate
Scissors Jump.job: Jumping moves: leg power and a fast heart rate.

Seated Cable Rows.job: Pulls toward your body, strengthening the upper back for posture.

Seated Calf Raise.job: Rises onto your toes, strengthening the calves and ankles.

Seated Floor Hamstring Stretch.job: Stretches the back of the thigh.

Seated Hamstring.job: Stretches the back of the thigh.

Seated Triceps Press.job: Straightens the elbow with the weight overhead, which stretches the triceps more; overhead work grew the triceps more in a study.

Shoulder Stretch.job: Stretches the back of the shoulder.

Side Lateral Raise.job: Lifts the arms out to the sides, isolating the side of the shoulder.

Side Leg Raises.job: Lifts your leg out to the side, working the muscles on the side of your hip.

Side Neck Stretch.job: Stretches the side of the neck.

Single Leg Glute Bridge.job: Drives your hips up, working the glutes with the knees bent.

Split Squats.area: Thighs and glutes, one leg at a time
Split Squats.job: Trains each leg on its own, for strength and balance.

Standing Calf Raises.job: Rises onto your toes, strengthening the calves and ankles.

Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise.job: Rises onto your toes, strengthening the calves and ankles.

Standing Hip Circles.job: Circles each hip to move it through its range.

Step-up with Knee Raise.area: Thighs and glutes, one leg at a time
Step-up with Knee Raise.job: Pushes your body up onto a step with one leg: strength and balance for stairs.

Stiff-Legged Dumbbell Deadlift.job: Hinges at the hips with a long stretch on the back of the thighs.

Superman.job: Lifts your chest and legs, strengthening the back side of your core.

Tricep Dumbbell Kickback.job: Straightens the elbow with your arm by your side.

Triceps Pushdown.job: Straightens the elbow with your arm by your side.

Triceps Stretch.job: Stretches the back of the upper arm.

Upper Back Stretch.job: Rounds and stretches the upper back.

Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown.area: Lats (sides of the back) and biceps
Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown.job: Pulls a bar down from overhead: the move that builds toward a pull-up.

abs.title: Want visible abs?
lines: This workout builds core strength and endurance. Ab moves alone did not shrink belly fat in studies.
Whether abs show depends on the fat over them, and that comes from moving more each day and eating a little less, not from more crunches.
Pair it with daily walking, keep 2 or more strength days a week so you keep muscle, and eat enough protein.
Big lifts like squats and lunges work your core too, so they count.

core.title: Want a strong core?
lines: This workout trains all sides of your core: the front (dead bug, plank), the sides (side bridge) and the back (superman, bridge).
For back pain, core work helped about as much as other kinds of exercise, so the best one is the one you'll keep doing.
It builds strength, not a smaller waist: that comes from losing fat overall.

arms.title: Want firmer, more defined arms?
lines: There's no separate toning workout: firmer arms come from building the muscle and losing fat overall. Arm moves alone don't burn arm fat.
Light or heavy weights both build muscle if the last 2 or 3 reps of each set are hard.
For the triceps (the back of the arm), one move with your arms overhead grew the muscle more in a study.
Work up to about 10 hard sets per muscle a week.

glutes.title: Want stronger, rounder glutes?
lines: Bridges, hip thrusts, squats and lunges all build the glutes. In one study, hip thrusts and squats grew the glutes about the same, and squats also grew the thighs more.
Add weight or reps over time: the same weight forever stops working.
Work up to about 10 hard sets for your glutes a week, over 2 days.

hips.title: Want looser hips and hamstrings?
lines: Flexibility builds with total time: at least about 5 minutes a week per area, with holds of 10 to 30 seconds.
Doing this 2 or 3 times a week gets you there; daily works best.
Strength moves through a full range (deep squats, long lunges, Romanian deadlifts) improved flexibility as much as stretching.

warmup.title: What this is for
lines: These are moving warm-ups: they get your joints going before a workout or a long day of sitting.
For more flexibility over time, you also need held stretches adding up to about 5 minutes a week per area, for example Hips and hamstrings.

muscle.title: Want to build muscle?
lines: Train each muscle on 2 days a week, working up to about 10 hard sets per muscle each week.
Light or heavy both work if the last 2 or 3 reps of each set are hard.
Add a rep or a little weight when you can, and eat about 1.6 g of protein per kg of body weight a day.

strength.title: Want to get stronger?
lines: Heavier weights gave the most strength gain. Rest longer between heavy sets: 3 to 5 minutes gave more strength than 1 minute.
Add a little weight once you beat your rep target 2 sessions in a row.
Do it on 2 or 3 days a week, with a day off between.

knees.title: Want knees that hurt less?
lines: Exercise eased knee pain and improved function for people with knee osteoarthritis.
Keep each move in a range that feels comfortable, and build up slowly.

skill.title: Building a skill
lines: Each move here builds strength in a part of the final skill. Practise on 2 or more days a week.
When you beat your target 2 sessions in a row, take the next step.

fitness.title: Want to feel fitter?
lines: Adults are advised to get 150 to 300 minutes of moderate activity a week, plus strength work on 2 days.
Short sessions like this one count toward both.

flexibility.title: Want to be more flexible?
lines: Flexibility builds with total time: at least about 5 minutes a week per area, with holds of 10 to 30 seconds.
Doing this 2 or 3 times a week gets you there; daily works best.
Strength moves through a full range improved flexibility as much as stretching, so your workouts help too.
When to expect change: strength usually comes first, in the first few weeks, as your body learns the moves.
Muscle growth starts early but is small at first; the studies behind these notes saw clear changes after 9 to 12 weeks.
